body:
> Found filing #207 on 2026-09-01. Its title begins with the word `--priority`, and `hkb create` answered with
> the bare usage line. Retitling the card was the only way through.

## Why

`parseArgs` (`src/cli.js:23-37`) treats any token starting with `--` as a flag, wherever it appears and whatever
it means, and accepts unknown flag names silently. Three consequences, in rising order of harm:

**1. A leading-`--` positional becomes a flag, and the error names nothing.**

```
parseArgs(["create", "--priority has no scale", "--triage"])
  → flags: { "priority has no scale": true, triage: true }   pos: ["create"]
```

`create` then finds no title and prints the generic usage line. Nothing says "your title looked like a flag",
so the fix is not discoverable from the message — value 5, every error says what to do next.

**2. `--` works, but only in one word order.** Line 28 `break`s, so *everything* after `--` is positional,
flags included: `create -- "--title" --triage` loses `--triage`. The working form is every flag first,
`--` last: `create --triage --paths a,b -- "--title"`. That is defensible, and it is documented nowhere.

**3. A flag *value* starting with `--` is silently dropped and replaced by a phantom flag.** This is the one
that corrupts data rather than refusing it:

```
parseArgs(["create", "title", "--goal", "--x marks it"])
  → flags: { goal: true, "x marks it": true }   pos: ["create", "title"]
```

The `--goal` value is gone, `goal` is now boolean `true`, and an invented flag stands in its place — with no
error at any layer, because unknown flags are never rejected. The same shape hits the terminal verbs, where the
payload is the protocol: `hkb finish 12 --summary "--force is gone from the docs"` files an attempt whose
summary silently vanished. `--summary-file` and `--from-stdin` exist precisely so the protocol does not depend
on shell quoting (`src/cli.js:41-44`), and this is the hole they were meant to close, still open on the inline
path.

Unknown-flag tolerance is what makes all three silent: `--prioritty 3` is accepted and dropped too.

## What

- **Reject unknown flags** per command, with the near-miss named (`--prioritty` → "did you mean --priority?").
  This is the fix that turns all three failures from silent into instructive, and it wants a per-command flag
  list — which `src/cli.js` already effectively has in its usage text.
- **A flag that takes a value must consume the next token**, whatever it starts with. Line 34's
  `!next.startsWith('--')` is guessing at intent; with a known flag list it does not have to guess. Keep the
  `BOOL_FLAGS` behaviour for flags that take none.
- **Say what happened when a positional looks like a flag.** If a command ends up with no title and an unknown
  flag whose name contains a space, that is this mistake: name it, and name `--` with the word order that works.
- **Document `--`** in the usage text for the commands that take free text (`create`, `comment`,
  `request-changes`, the terminal verbs).
- Pure parsing decisions belong in `src/model.js` per the layout rule; `parseArgs` stays the thin caller.
  Tests go in `test/args.test.js`, which already covers this function.

## Done when

- [ ] `hkb create "--anything" ...` either works or fails with a message naming the cause and the `--` form.
- [ ] `hkb finish 12 --summary "--x"` files `--x` as the summary, or refuses; it never files an empty one.
- [ ] An unknown or misspelled flag is an error, not a silent drop, on every command.
- [ ] `test/args.test.js` covers a leading-`--` positional, a `--`-prefixed flag value, and a misspelled flag.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass.
goal: A leading-dash positional and a dash-prefixed flag value either work or fail with a message naming the cause and the -- form; an unknown or misspelled flag is an error rather than a silent drop; test/args.test.js covers all three
title: A title or flag value that starts with two dashes is silently eaten by parseArgs, and an unknown flag is never rejected
